core_question: Should SkyNet proceed with the urban drone delivery launch in Q3 2025, and if so, which fleet configuration (Heavy-Lifter v2 or Swift-Class) is more financially and operationally viable?
central_thesis: The storyline should be led by the strongest public evidence, then translated into management choices.
narrative_focus: Evidence is densest around: source quality, timing, commercial proof
structure_logic: Open with the executive decision, show source-backed data exhibits, then move through business implications, risks and action gates.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Consumer willingness to pay for drone delivery is at least $5 per delivery in urban areas, sufficient to cover variable costs.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Validates revenue model; if false, pricing strategy must change or launch is unviable.
needed_evidence: Survey data or pilot studies showing WTP; actual transaction data from competitors.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Heavy-Lifter v2 has a lower total cost per delivery than Swift-Class when factoring in payload capacity and maintenance.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Determines fleet choice; if false, Swift-Class may be preferred despite higher unit cost.
needed_evidence: Manufacturer specs, maintenance records, operational cost data from similar drones.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: FAA will approve UAM corridor operations for drone delivery in at least 3 major US cities by Q3 2025.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Regulatory risk; if false, launch must be delayed or limited to non-US markets.
needed_evidence: FAA rulemaking timelines, pilot program announcements, expert interviews.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: The total addressable market for urban drone delivery in the US is at least $5 billion by 2026.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Market size justifies investment; if false, scale back or pivot.
needed_evidence: Industry reports, analyst forecasts, comparable market data.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Noise complaints from drone operations will not exceed 10% of residents in target neighborhoods.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Social license to operate; if false, need mitigation or route changes.
needed_evidence: Noise studies, community surveys, data from existing drone operations.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Heavy-Lifter v2 can achieve a 99.5% mission completion rate in urban environments.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Reliability affects customer satisfaction and cost; if false, need redundancy or choose Swift-Class.
needed_evidence: Test flight data, reliability reports from similar drones, failure rate analysis.

hypotheses_to_test.hypothesis: Insurance premiums for urban drone delivery fleets will be less than 5% of revenue.
hypotheses_to_test.decision_relevance: Cost factor; if false, profitability may be eroded.
needed_evidence: Insurance quotes, industry benchmarks, risk assessment reports.

market_sizing_logic.formula: TAM = (Number of urban households in target cities) * (Average annual delivery spend per household) * (Drone delivery penetration rate)
variables: Urban households in top 10 US cities
Average annual delivery spend per household (e.g., $200)

market_sizing_logic.formula: TAM = (Number of drones deployed) * (Deliveries per drone per day) * (Average revenue per delivery) * 365
TAM = (Total last-mile delivery market value) * (Drone-addressable share)
variables: Total US last-mile delivery market value (e.g., $150B)

market_sizing_logic.formula: TAM = (Maximum drone deliveries possible given regulatory and infrastructure constraints) * (Average revenue per delivery)

charting_rule: Charts may use only evidence_ledger values, dates, source counts or same-unit comparable values tied to public URLs.
exhibit_narrative_rule: Every exhibit must be embedded in the section argument: prose sets up the management question before the exhibit and interprets the implication after it; never stack exhibits without prose.
